inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(58,57) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(58,57) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 57 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 57: a host write to 57 is overwritten on the next update. Two physical flippers share this cabinet chain.

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 10 is the outhole, 11 and 12 the two trough positions, and 14 the shooter lane. Coil 1 transfers the drain and coil 2 feeds the shooter; script starts with two balls.
mechanisms.label: Two-ball trough and feeder

mechanisms.behavior: Lock lane 38 leads to the visible lock: 40 is front and 39 rear. Coil 8 releases its gate; it does not directly actuate the ball sensors.
mechanisms.label: Two-position ball lock

mechanisms.behavior: Three optical down sensors remain active while targets are down; coil 6 and the shared reset plate restore the bank. C-11223-4 contains optical board C-13205-1; both whole parts tables are retained. The table's sounds and target reset timing are implementation tuning, not measured machine motion.
mechanisms.label: Bottom three-drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Three optical down sensors remain active while targets are down; coil 4 and the shared reset plate restore the bank. C-11223-4 contains optical board C-13205-1. Targets can jam individually; the reset actuator restores the bank together.
mechanisms.label: Top three-drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: One enabled pulse toggles the two-position latch through its flat cam; switch 20 reports position. The script alternates DiverterDown/Up and public20 only on the enabled edge; its initial wall pose is a table startup choice, not a measured factory home. No travel time is measured. A stuck microswitch can misreport which ramp branch is selected.
mechanisms.label: Bowtie diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Left outlane switch 51 and coil 14 serve the kickback.
mechanisms.label: Left outlane kickback

mechanisms.behavior: Four physical flippers in two cabinet button chains. Outputs 45-48 are synthetic states, not individual windings or EOS outputs.
mechanisms.label: Four flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Four jet and two sling assemblies use special drivers 1-6, published at 17-22. The own-ROM isolated score-contact probes produce52->17,55->18,53->19,56->20,54->21,50->22. These prove the ROM response, not physical kick-contact topology or measured mechanical latency.
mechanisms.label: Four jets and two slings

mechanisms.behavior: Ball-driven spinners coast by inertia; there is no motor actuator.
mechanisms.label: Top and right spinners
